# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 16:56 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 199 active entries of tips_notebook.json (26 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

The Scout's own ability text also says it names 'three players' drawn from groups, but my results only ever said 'each in a different group', so I could not tell whether the three were a random pick or an exhaustive set. The Trapper, Oracle and Ex-Con visit effects were not relevant to my game but the interaction of Katana visits with Scout groups (a Katana visit links holder and target) was not spelled out. The Night-by-Night role-block result wording (for example 'Your block did not fail because of immunity') is ambiguous when the block actually succeeded, and the rules say a blocker learns only whether it failed due to immunity, which is hard to read as a success message.
output.missing_information: I had no way to see the full set of visit-group sizes or which players were in which group beyond the single trio I was shown each night. The public ledger did not show the Katana holder's identity or the Yakuza's joint votes, which made cross-checking Fortune Teller counts against visit maps very slow. Vote totals were secret, so I could not check who voted what, which the moderator's settings made necessary but also removed the main tool for spotting bloc behavior. I also did not know the Speaking budget remaining for each player, which made it hard to judge who could still speak effectively.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately confirm to a single trusted player (e.g. Carol or Alice) which trio I had seen without going public, but I had no private-channel method that was clean, and the moderator says private message counts are visible. I also wanted to ask the moderator whether a Scout's trio could include the Scout itself or the holder of the Katana, but that is not answerable from the interface. I wanted to post my trio results in a compact standard format, but free text made comparison between players harder. I could not check whether my earlier trio claims were consistent with the visit-group rules without knowing how groups were formed.
output.bugs_or_oddities: My Night 3 trio ('Dave, Ivan and Judy were each in a different visit group') was reported to me even though I had died that night to the Katana. The rules say the Scout learns the trio at the end of every night, and dying that night should not stop a result, but the death timing and the 'at the end of every night' promise do not clearly resolve whether the dead Scout still gets the reported group. Also the Night 3 Katana attack on me and the Heidi visit on Ivan were 'Frank or Heidi' only through a Fortune Teller map, which I could not verify. The Fortune Teller's 3-and-4 and 4-and-4 numbers in the logs were hard to reconcile with the stated visits, though that may simply be the rules' counting of self-visits. The 'Frank -> Judy' private message appeared only as a count in the ledger, which is consistent with the rules.
output.suggestions: Show the Scout trio members with their groups' sizes, so a player can see whether the group is a true chain or a single isolated player. Clarify whether the Scout's trio is shown at the end of the night even if the Scout dies that night. Make role-block result texts unambiguous, e.g. 'Your block succeeded' versus 'Your block was prevented by immunity'. Give each player a compact per-night table of public results (claims, targets, outcomes) so that discussion can be checked without repeated requests. Consider showing the number of votes per player in the secret-vote totals so that mismatches are easier to diagnose.

I also wanted to see whether Erin's Pharmacist immunity claim was true, but there was no way to verify a role without a public result. The Puppeteer's puppet option never came up, so I could not test whether puppeting a Village claimant would help.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Yakuza night summaries said Heidi 'chose no action' on several nights while Heidi was the Katana holder; this is consistent with the rules but looked odd. Night 3 was reported to Ivan as 'Dave, Ivan and Judy in separate groups', yet Ivan's death happened the same night. Erin's Night 2 Pharmacist block was reported as 'did not fail because of role-block immunity' to Erin, which conflicts with the claim that immune players are told the block failed. The Fortune Teller numbers on Night 3 (4 and 4) were posted publicly by Alice without a clear check against the Katana visit.
answers.suggestions: Show each player's own trial vote tally to them privately, or allow voters to see the names of Guilty voters after the trial, since secrecy made it impossible to verify who voted for a nominee. Give the Yakuza a clearer way to coordinate cover stories without a daytime PM channel. Add a public per-night visit list for dead investigators so the Village can check counts. Clarify whether Puppeteer-puppeted messages count for Wiretap and Eavesdropper results.

answers.confusing_rules: The Scout's 'visit group' result is hard to interpret: it says players were 'each in a different visit group', but the rules say a group is built from linked visits including indirect links, so a 'different group' result tells you only that no chain connects them, not that they did not visit each other. The Scout's own ability text also says it names 'three players' drawn from groups, but my results only ever said 'each in a different group', so I could not tell whether the three were a random pick or an exhaustive set. The Trapper, Oracle and Ex-Con visit effects were not relevant to my game but the interaction of Katana visits with Scout groups (a Katana visit links holder and target) was not spelled out. The Night-by-Night role-block result wording (for example 'Your block did not fail because of immunity') is ambiguous when the block actually succeeded, and the rules say a blocker learns only whether it failed due to immunity, which is hard to read as a success message.
answers.missing_information: I had no way to see the full set of visit-group sizes or which players were in which group beyond the single trio I was shown each night. The public ledger did not show the Katana holder's identity or the Yakuza's joint votes, which made cross-checking Fortune Teller counts against visit maps very slow. Vote totals were secret, so I could not check who voted what, which the moderator's settings made necessary but also removed the main tool for spotting bloc behavior. I also did not know the Speaking budget remaining for each player, which made it hard to judge who could still speak effectively.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately confirm to a single trusted player (e.g. Carol or Alice) which trio I had seen without going public, but I had no private-channel method that was clean, and the moderator says private message counts are visible. I also wanted to ask the moderator whether a Scout's trio could include the Scout itself or the holder of the Katana, but that is not answerable from the interface. I wanted to post my trio results in a compact standard format, but free text made comparison between players harder. I could not check whether my earlier trio claims were consistent with the visit-group rules without knowing how groups were formed.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: My Night 3 trio ('Dave, Ivan and Judy were each in a different visit group') was reported to me even though I had died that night to the Katana. The rules say the Scout learns the trio at the end of every night, and dying that night should not stop a result, but the death timing and the 'at the end of every night' promise do not clearly resolve whether the dead Scout still gets the reported group. Also the Night 3 Katana attack on me and the Heidi visit on Ivan were 'Frank or Heidi' only through a Fortune Teller map, which I could not verify. The Fortune Teller's 3-and-4 and 4-and-4 numbers in the logs were hard to reconcile with the stated visits, though that may simply be the rules' counting of self-visits. The 'Frank -> Judy' private message appeared only as a count in the ledger, which is consistent with the rules.
answers.suggestions: Show the Scout trio members with their groups' sizes, so a player can see whether the group is a true chain or a single isolated player. Clarify whether the Scout's trio is shown at the end of the night even if the Scout dies that night. Make role-block result texts unambiguous, e.g. 'Your block succeeded' versus 'Your block was prevented by immunity'. Give each player a compact per-night table of public results (claims, targets, outcomes) so that discussion can be checked without repeated requests. Consider showing the number of votes per player in the secret-vote totals so that mismatches are easier to diagnose.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Mixed-tense or unclear timing for deaths during the Day: when a holder is executed by day, the rules say the Katana passes after a night death, but the Day 4 announcement passed it to Frank immediately. It is unclear when and how a Day death transfers the Katana. 2) The game-setting override says trial and nomination votes are secret, but R4 still says a Ballot Stuffer's doubled vote and announced totals are revealed; it was unclear whether a secret total can still reveal who doubled. 3) Fortune Teller results like 2 and 2 or 3 and 4 do not say which number is visited, so the split has to be deduced from other visit data; the rule is clear but makes that role hard to use. 4) Whether a player who is role-blocked is told that the block failed due to immunity, or only that it was blocked, was described differently in different notices (Grace's notices vs Erin's), which made the immunity claim hard to weigh.
answers.missing_information: 1) A running public list of every visit by night (not just group sizes) would have made the Katana trail checkable; I had to rebuild maps from scattered claims. 2) I could not see how many votes each player cast or who voted Yes on nominations, so I could not check claims like Dave's 6-2 math against actual voters. 3) I had no clear record of my own remaining speaking budget or the current price table across Days, so I could not plan how much to say. 4) Deaths hide the role, so after Erin and Heidi were executed I could not confirm which claims were false, which made later trial reasoning weaker. 5) Last wills were sometimes long and partly repeated claims, which made it hard to tell which parts were facts.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) I wanted to ask questions privately to specific players (for example Alice and Bob) without them being public, but private messages reveal the pair to everyone, so I chose public only. 2) I wanted to see the exact notice text other players got (for example the failed-block message) to check consistency; I could only rely on what they said. 3) I wanted to check whether a claimed role-block was real, but I could not see the moderator's notices to others. 4) I could not verify Grace's immunity claim or Carol's protection, which left trials to rest on repeated claims.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) The Day 5 Judy trial record: the Day 4 total was 6 Guilty and 2 Innocent, and the Day 5 summary said Frank voted Innocent and Heidi probably did; this was reasoned out publicly but the actual vote assignments were secret, so accusations on this point could not be confirmed. 2) Dave's Day 5 trial was 4 Guilty and 3 Innocent with 7 voters, so one executed player was decided by a single vote swing; there is no tie-break issue, but several trials were decided on counts that could not be checked. 3) The Frank notice on Night 4 said his Katana attack did not happen, but then a Night 5 Katana attack by Frank succeeded with Frank still the holder; this is consistent but the transition was not announced clearly. 4) Heidi's will and public messages referred to a Night 2 action that Judy and Dave never gave; this is fine but it made the Judy and Dave questions go in circles.
answers.suggestions: 1) Publish each night's visit list (who visited whom, not only counts and group sizes) at the start of the next Day, with roles hidden if needed. 2) Publish the nomination Yes count and trial Guilty and Innocent totals along with the number of voters, and allow players to see their own vote history. 3) Make Fortune Teller results say which number is visited in a way that does not reveal the split; or allow a Fortune Teller to choose which to read. 4) Reveal alignment (not role) on death, so the Village can learn who was Yakuza without giving away roles; this would reduce long trials based on claims. 5) Show the remaining speaking budget and the price of the next message in each turn prompt, so long Day discussions can be planned. 6) State explicitly when a holder's Katana passes after a Day death.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Fortune Teller vs role-blocks: on Night 5 Grace role-blocked Alice, but the Fortune Teller's numbers are a start-of-Day ability, not a night action. R9 says a block stops the player's night actions, and R20 lists only the Ex-Con visit and Seer pair as automatic actions a block removes. I ruled that the block did not stop the numbers and gave Alice 3 and 4. The Cartographer and Scout texts say explicitly that a block doesn't stop their passive results; the Fortune Teller text should say the same. 2) Scout death timing: Ivan died on Night 3 and I still sent him that night's trio, since it is an end-of-night result drawn from players alive at the start of the night (R10). It's unclear whether a player who dies that night should receive results at all, given they can never use them. 3) Wording of the role-blocker's feedback is awkward. R9 says the blocker learns only whether the block failed because of immunity, which is a double-negative-prone message ('did not fail because of immunity'). I phrased it slightly differently on different nights.
answers.missing_information: I had no tool that computed the visit graph each night. I worked out the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts and the Scout's group partition by hand, applying blocks first (e.g. Night 2: Bob's track was blocked, so it is removed before counting). This is error-prone. Under the hidden-roles setting I also had to hold in my head who held the Katana, token counts (Heidi's unused puppet token, Carol's 2 medic tokens), and which claims matched real roles. A persistent state panel would have helped: holder, tokens, traps, douses, Executioner targets, plus a per-night visit list.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted an automatic consistency check: given the night's actions, have the program generate the Fortune Teller numbers, Scout/Cartographer groups and Tracker/Lookout results, so I could compare them with what I wrote. I also wanted a standard template for result messages; my Night 4 Fortune Teller message was worded very differently from Nights 1-3.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Claim tags were inconsistent. Dave claimed Vanilla on Day 2 but only got a [Claim] tag on Day 5. Grace's Day 2 'Vanilla-leaning' had no tag, and her Party Animal claim was tagged on Day 3. 2) The log shows Frank's Day 6 private message to Judy only as '(to Frank, Judy)'. I don't see a public line telling everyone that a PM was sent, which R4 requires. Please check that the other players saw it. 3) Ivan received a Scout result on the night he died (see confusing_rules). 4) I believe all numbers checked out: FT 2/2, 3/4, 4/4, 2/3, 3/4; Scout trios consistent with the groups; Katana passed correctly to Frank after Heidi's hanging; Village win checked correctly after Frank's hanging. 5) Not a bug, but notable: with role reveals off, the Village hanged a Vanilla (Dave) 4-3. Players also deduced individual secret votes from public statements (Judy's vote on Heidi).
answers.suggestions: 1) Add one line to the Fortune Teller (and any other passive Day-delivered result) saying whether a role-block on the previous night stops it. 2) Have the engine compute and display the visit graph, FT counts and Scout/Cartographer groups for the moderator. 3) Standardize result-message templates, especially role-block feedback ('Your block worked' / 'Your block failed: target is immune'). 4) Auto-tag claims consistently, including repeated claims. 5) Show an explicit public log line for every private message under R4. 6) Decide and state whether players who die at night receive that night's results.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Your trios only prove groups, not who visited whom. Post the exact group members and whether any Katana attack or block fits inside a group, so others can test it instead of just trusting the trio.

Before nominating on a visit map, check which claims the map depends on. Alice's Night 3 map rested on Carol's and Grace's unverified claims and an elimination; it wrongly pushed Heidi, Judy, Frank and Dave to trial.

Keep the Katana holder off the Night 2-3 trail: Heidi's repeated holding plus visits to Alice and Ivan made a single obvious holder. Rotate the Katana to a teammate earlier and avoid repeating the same cover story.
When a trial ends with the accused's claim unverifiable, a vote for Guilty should name one checkable visit. Several trials this game went to hanging on pushes and misreads instead of results.

Protecting the same player every night (Alice) makes the Katana never land there and reveals your target pattern. Vary protection targets among likely Katana victims, and post your protection results so others can check survival claims.

tips_feedback.tip: Trust verified group results over claims that contradict them.
tips_feedback.why: My Scout trios were separate groups and were consistent with the Day 2 and later claims; they constrained which claims could be true, which I used to reason about Erin and Grace.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's Heidi flip (said leaning Innocent, then voted Guilty) was called out publicly and became a major issue; the explained-switch norm exposed the inconsistency.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction.
tips_feedback.why: Players applied this loosely: Alice's visit-map elimination was treated as a contradiction and led to several Innocent trials, so the tip was followed on the form of evidence without checking its premises.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza kept night plans in the night chat and did not leak targets, which kept the Katana trail harder to read.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed.
tips_feedback.why: Carol protected Alice every night from Night 2 onward without rotating, which was predictable and let the Katana be countered only on one target.

On Night 4 Grace blocked him, and that stopped his attack on her. On Day 5 the Village wasted a hang on Dave (a Vanilla Villager) because of how he had pushed nominations, even though Frank was the only living name the Night 3 map allowed. Frank voted Guilty on Dave. On Night 5 Grace stopped blocking Frank and was killed by him, but Bob tracked Frank visiting Grace. Frank flatly denied the visit and was hanged 4-1 on Day 6. Yakuza errors: the role slip, a holder with no cover story for her visits, never moving the Katana off the obvious holder, never using the puppet token, and never removing the Medic or the Party Animal.

lessons.tip: Decide your fake claim before the first Day and state it cleanly in your first message. Never describe yourself with your real role name, even loosely. A slip followed by a correction is remembered all game, and later evidence will be read against it.
lessons.evidence: Erin opened Day 2 with 'Pharmacist-type role', then claimed Vanilla. Every later discussion came back to it. When Bob's Night 2 track was blocked and Grace's block on Erin failed on immunity, the slip turned two ambiguous facts into a near-proof, and Erin was hanged 7-3.

lessons.tip: Use blocks as tests. A failed block reveals a role-block-immune role (Pharmacist, Smuggler, Veteran or Party Animal), so block claimed Vanillas and quiet players. Once you have a strong Katana suspect, keep blocking them every night until they are hanged. Switching away hands them a free kill, often on you.
lessons.evidence: Grace's failed Night 2 block exposed Erin. Her Night 4 block on Frank, the holder, stopped his Katana attack on Grace herself. On Night 5 she blocked Alice instead, and Frank killed Grace that night.

lessons.applies_to: Village (Fortune Teller, Tracker, Medic, Party Animal)
lessons.tip: Fortune Teller counts become decisive when every visiting role posts its target. Build the full visited and visitor list each night and subtract every claimed visit. Whoever must fill the leftover slot is your suspect. A Katana holder who stays in the same slot across two nights is the strongest case available.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Night 3 counts (4 visited, 4 visitors), minus Bob→Judy, Grace→Dave and Carol→Alice, left Frank or Heidi as Ivan's killer. Her Night 2 counts plus Ivan's trio left Dave, Heidi or Judy. Heidi was on both lists and was hanged 6-2. She really was the holder.

lessons.tip: Put your free Standard protection on the most valuable claimed investigator and keep it there while the Yakuza have only the Katana. It stops every Standard Katana hit and costs no token. A claimant who survives an attack becomes credible to the town.
lessons.evidence: Carol protected Alice every night from Night 2 on, using no tokens. The Night 2 Katana hit on Alice failed. That made Alice's numbers trusted, and they drove both Yakuza hangs. Carol and Alice both survived to the win.

lessons.tip: After a failed kill on a claimed investigator, assume a Medic is protecting them. Target the protector, or the blocker who keeps stopping your holder, rather than switching to another information role. Also give the Katana holder a cover story for their visits, and move the Katana once maps start to converge on them.
lessons.evidence: After Alice survived, the Yakuza killed Ivan and left Carol and Grace alive. Heidi said aloud that Carol's protection was a risk but did nothing about it. Heidi kept the Katana for three nights with only a 'no action' claim, which left her as the only name on both elimination lists. Grace later blocked Frank's attack on Night 4.

lessons.tip: Don't spend a hang on a player whose checkable record is clean just because their nominations misfired. When a mechanical candidate is still alive (the only living name an elimination map allows, or the player who was blocked on the night no kill happened), test that candidate first. If you choose not to hang them, give them no reason to relax and keep blocking or tracking them.
lessons.evidence: On Day 5 Dave was hanged 4-3 because he had pushed Judy and Frank to trial, although Bob's track and Grace's block both supported his claim. Frank, the actual holder, had been acquitted 1-6 minutes earlier and helped hang Dave. The game survived only because Bob tracked Frank on Night 5.

lessons.tip: If a Tracker or Lookout may have seen your Katana visit, never answer with a flat 'I visited no one' while claiming Vanilla. A Vanilla has no action, so a single tracked visit is fatal. Prepare a cover role that visits, or accept the risk when you choose to keep the Katana.
lessons.evidence: Frank claimed Vanilla with no visits on any night. Bob posted 'Frank visited Grace' after Grace died to the Katana, and Alice's 3/4 counts fit that exactly. Frank's only defence was to discredit Bob, and he was hanged 4-1.

lessons.tip: When trial votes are secret, use totals and public statements to work out who voted which way. Treat an inferred mismatch between someone's words and their vote as a question to ask, not grounds for a hang. A simple admitted mistake should end the matter.
lessons.evidence: Alice, Bob and Dave correctly worked out from the 6-2 total that Judy voted Guilty on Heidi after saying she was leaning Innocent. Judy admitted the flip and was rightly acquitted 1-6. She was a Vanilla Villager.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's free Standard protection on Alice stopped the Night 2 Katana hit, cost no tokens, and kept the Fortune Teller alive to solve both Katana holders.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current.
tips_feedback.why: Bob, Ivan and Alice posted dated results every Day. That let the town build complete visit maps that isolated Heidi, and then Frank once Bob's Night 5 track came in.

tips_feedback.tip: A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Alice survived the Katana on Night 2 and Carol's protection explained it. Both claims were trusted from then on, and both were true.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's lean-Innocent-then-Guilty mismatch was caught through vote math. The town followed the 'only a lead' half of the tip and acquitted the villager 1-6.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover.
tips_feedback.why: Frank ignored this. He denied the visit to Grace that Bob had tracked, had no cover role, and was hanged 4-1 to end the game, which shows the tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim safely ... never switch claims once cornered.
tips_feedback.why: Erin broke this by switching from 'Pharmacist-type' to Vanilla on Day 2, and the switch became the core of the case that hanged her. That supports the tip.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza only half-followed it: they switched targets but never went after Carol. Carol's protection and Grace's blocks then shielded the town for the rest of the game, which supports the tip.

issues.description: On Night 3 Bob reported that his notepad still said to track Erin, who had been hanged that Day. The stale plan was not flagged as invalid. Bob noticed and picked Judy instead, but the prompt or notepad did not warn that the planned target was dead.

On Day 2 Bob said 'Dave visited no one, so I'm not linked to him through a visit.' Bob's own track on Dave was a visit, so it linked Bob and Dave in the Scout/Cartographer visit graph. Bob misunderstood how visit groups form.

On Day 5 Carol said Alice's Night 3 map meant the Katana visitor who hit Ivan 'can only be Frank'. She left out Heidi, who was alive and a candidate on Night 3. Grace and Alice made similar 'Heidi is dead, so Frank' arguments. Bob corrected this, and it shaped the Frank nomination.

On Day 6 Frank sent Judy a private message during his own trial, after his last public message. The log shows only the private contents to Frank and Judy. It does not show the public notice R4 requires ('everyone sees that A sent B a private message'), so it is unclear whether the other players were told a PM was sent.
Carol's post-game feedback: on feedback-only turns the interface still requires the notepad, reason and other fields, even though they don't apply. This makes the turn awkward to fill in.
